briefdescription.para: Factor by which the viscous stress is degraded as the material loses stiffness.

detaileddescription.para:
currentWaveSpeed
Wave speed of the material at its CURRENT state, i.e. from the algorithmic tangent as it is now.
referenceWaveSpeed
Wave speed of the same material in its virgin state.
exponent
The exponent $n$. Zero returns exactly one.
$\left(c/c_0\right)^n$, clamped to $[0,1]$.
A fully cracked element carries no real stress, but the linear term keeps transmitting $b_1\rho c_0 L_e \dot{\varepsilon}_\mathrm{vol}$ across the crack. Being active in expansion, it resists the crack OPENING and never relaxes, and its work is charged to the fracture energy: measured on a gradient-damage bar, bulk viscosity at the Abaqus/Explicit coefficients inflated $G_f$ by 27 to 55 percent, while applying it everywhere EXCEPT the damaged elements changed $G_f$ by -1.6 percent. This is the argument that already restricts the quadratic term to compression, applied to the STATE rather than to the sign of the rate.

The wave-speed ratio is the square root of the tangent-stiffness ratio, so for a tangent degrading as $(1-\omega)\,\mathbb{C}_0$: $n = 1$ scales with $\sqrt{1-\omega}$, $n = 2$ with $1-\omega$ itself, and $n = 0$ never evaluates the current wave speed at all.

simplesect.para: It degrades with the current TANGENT, not with a damage variable no material interface here reports damage. For a quasi-brittle material in tension the two coincide; for one that merely yields, the viscous stress is degraded by plastic flow rather than cracking.

Not free: the current wave speed is asked of the material on every quadrature point on every increment, which is why the reference is cached and why this is opt-in. With the material interface's default getMaximumWaveSpeed() that query is a full constitutive evaluation about the cost of the stress update itself on a non-yielding point so a damage model meant to run with this should override it with its closed form, and check the override against the default with Marmot::Testing::checkMaximumWaveSpeedOverrideMatchesDefault().

memberdef.argsstring: (double volumetricStrainRate, double density, double waveSpeed, double characteristicElementLength, const Coefficients &coefficients)
memberdef.name: viscousStress

briefdescription.para: The artificial viscous stress added to every normal stress component.

parameterdescription.para: Trace of the strain rate, $\dot{\varepsilon}_\mathrm{vol} = \mathrm{tr}(\dot{\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}})$. Negative in compression.

Current mass density $\rho$. If the run is mass scaled, this is the SCALED density, which is correct: the term exists to damp the modes of the system that is actually being integrated, and mass scaling changes those.
Dilatational wave speed $c_d$ of the material.

simplesect.para: The scalar $\sigma_\mathrm{bv}$ to ADD to $\sigma_{xx}$, $\sigma_{yy}$ and $\sigma_{zz}$ (i.e. $\boldsymbol{\sigma}_\mathrm{bv} = \sigma_\mathrm{bv}\, \mathbf{I}$). Deviatoric components are untouched.

detaileddescription.para: following the standard element-level artificial viscosity of

listitem.para: VonNeumann, J. & Richtmyer, R. D. (1950). "A method for the numerical calculation of hydrodynamic shocks". Journal of Applied Physics 21(3), 232-237. https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1699639
Landshoff, R. (1955). "A numerical method for treating fluid flow in the presence of shocks". Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory report LA-1930.

detaileddescription.para: as applied in explicit finite element codes (Abaqus/Explicit, LS-DYNA): the linear (Landshoff) term damps element-level ringing, the quadratic (Von Neumann-Richtmyer) term spreads a shock over a few elements.

A numerical device, not a material model. It adds no state, is not seen by the constitutive law and never enters the stored stress only the stress that is integrated. Both terms are dissipative by construction, so it can only remove energy.

The quadratic term is restricted to compression, where in expansion it would resist a crack or void opening. The linear term is not: damping one sign of the volumetric rate only would rectify the ringing it exists to remove into a net volumetric drift.

simplesect.para: $L_e$ must be the same characteristic length the stable time increment is computed from. Both scale the term to the highest frequency the mesh can carry, and if they disagree the damping is no longer tied to the mode it is meant to damp.

memberdef.argsstring: (double volumetricStrainIncrement, double timeIncrement, double density, double waveSpeed, double characteristicElementLength, const Coefficients &coefficients)
memberdef.name: viscousStressFromIncrement

briefdescription.para: The artificial viscous stress from a strain INCREMENT rather than a rate.

detaileddescription.para:
volumetricStrainIncrement
Trace of the strain increment of the current time increment.
timeIncrement
The time increment $\Delta t$ it was taken over.
density
Current mass density $\rho$.
waveSpeed
Dilatational wave speed $c_d$ of the material.
characteristicElementLength
The element's smallest physical extent $L_e$.
coefficients
The two dimensionless coefficients.
The scalar $\sigma_\mathrm{bv}$ to add to the normal stress components.
Convenience overload for an explicit element, which has the strain increment at hand and not the rate. A non-positive $\Delta t$ yields exactly zero rather than an infinity: an explicit solver legitimately calls its elements with $\Delta t = 0$ to prime the internal force at the start of a step, and a viscous stress is not defined there.
